## What We Did

<!-- CHANGE THIS: replace with your own notes -->

What is a Website?

  a. a folder of html files + a computer that is   always on
  b. we are going to be using Quarto + GitHub

What is Quarto?
  a.makes .qmd files that you write → magic       quarto machine →   html files
  b.magic is made by clicking render
  c.what happens in the machine —
      1. reads the file from top to bottom
      2. finds the code chunks
      3. sends them to R, gets results 
      4. glues the text + the results into html
  d. if there is an error the magic does not          happen
Anatomy of a .qmd

Files + Folders
  a. Who is this file for?
  b.For me files vs For the machine

For me
  index.qmd
  about.qmd
  weekly_notes/*.qmd
  assignments/*.qmd
For machine
  _quarto.yml (settings for the whole website)
  _freeze/   (for quarto after it gets rendered **Do not touch**)
  .Rproj → Rstudio
  .gitignore → Github
  .renviron → R (secrets)
  docs/  → the internet i.e. where your website     lives

“Index”
  a. website rule: ask for a folder, you get     that folder index.html
  b. carennakt.github.io/  → docs/index.html
 /weekly-notes → docs/weekly.notes/index.html

GIT/GitHub.com/GitHub desktop
  a. GIT is a version tracker, invisible, runs    on your computer
    i. commit → “save a labeled snapshot” (lives       on your computer)
    ii. push → “send my snapshot to GitHub.com”
  b.GitHub.com is a website that stores a copy    of your folder   c.GitHub desktop are buttons   that tell GIT what to do 
  
.Rscript

  b.sandbox
  c.good for working out the problems,              experimenting, sketch   book 
  d. In console you can run stuff real quick but     it doesnt save repository is like a larger      folder that you wanna share w the world on      github

Workflow

## Key Concepts

Three places a file can live:

1. **My computer** — where I edit
2. **GitHub.com** — where it's stored
3. **My live site** — what the world sees

The loop: **Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh**

## Proving R Works

The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath
it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.

```{r}
sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string
```
